Subject: FinTechCo - RTBF / Delete request workflow (post-demo follow-up)

Hi John —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Per our call, you asked for a written summary of how Redwood handles customer deletion/Right to be Forgotten (RTBF) requests and the practical constraints around backups/audits. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps.

Recap (what we covered)
- Immediate deletion: We provide a delete API that can target a customer account or specific data objects. On acceptance, we remove active objects, session caches, and any token/KV caches used by the runtime.
- Logs & audit: We retain structured audit logs (request traces, timestamps) for security and billing; these can be redacted or pseudonymized on a per-customer basis. Raw user messages are not stored in plaintext in long-term logs by default.
- Backups & snapshots: Cold backups / object-store snapshots may persist beyond the active deletion window (typical snapshot lifecycle depends on retention policies). We discussed a reasonable SLA (30–90 days) for full propagation across backup layers, with the option for shorter timelines on dedicated/private deployments.
- Data residency: We can ensure deletion occurs within the region where the data lives; we support region-specific workflows for EU/US/APAC.

Constraints & options we discussed
- Backups: For hosted customers on shared infrastructure, we can schedule expedited purges of customer objects from incremental backups on a best-effort basis; however, immutable external-provider snapshots (e.g., multi-day archival backups) may require additional contractual terms.
- Auditability: We emit deletion audit events and can provide signed receipts for completed purges.

Attachments: I attached our draft RTBF delete flow (RTBF-delete-flow-v1.pdf) and a technical API spec for deletion events (deletion-api-spec.yaml).

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm the exact scope of the request (account-level vs. dataset vs. user-id).
2) Marcus will follow up with a short technical note on timelines for backups and any potential impacts on analytics/derived datasets.
3) If you want, we can put a 30-minute call on calendar next week to align on SLA language for the contract.

If you confirm the scope, we’ll turn this into an actionable mutual action plan (MAP) and a documented SLA item for the deal.

Thanks,
Camila

Hi John — quick technical follow-up as promised. Short answers first, then details.

Short answers
- Can Redwood meet a 30-day SLA across active + backups? For hosted/shared tiers: we can commit to deleting active objects and caches within 48 hours and removing customer objects from primary object stores within 7 days. Full propagation to all cold backups/snapshots is typically 30–90 days depending on snapshot cadence and retention. For Dedicated/Private deployments (reserved capacity or VPC), we can negotiate contractual terms for <30 day full purge.
- Auditable receipts: Yes — we produce deletion events with hashes and timestamps; we can generate a signed PDF receipt on completion.

Details / technical notes
1) Active data: deletion API removes primary objects (S3 keys, DB rows) and purges runtime caches. This process is synchronous and completes in minutes for normal volumes.
2) Incremental backups: our daily incremental backups will stop referencing deleted keys within the next incremental window; however, depending on the retention window, the physical bytes may persist in archive tiers until compaction/retention expiry.
3) Immutable snapshots & third-party backups: if a customer requests guaranteed immediate removal from immutable external snapshots, we need a contractual commitment and potentially a provider-side assistance (e.g., cloud provider snapshot deletion). This is typically handled as an exception with a short SLA and possible cost to cover manual operations.
4) Derived datasets & analytics: deletion cascades to primary derived tables if they are built deterministically from source keys; non-deterministic/aggregates may need re-computation or redaction policies.
5) Audit trail: deletion events, user IDs impacted, and internal ticket IDs are recorded. We can provide mechanisms for data subject requests to include the deletion ticket ID.

Suggested MAP items
- Confirm scope (account vs user IDs) and any regulatory constraints (GDPR-specific wording).
- Choose target SLA for full purge (30d standard, 15d expedited for Dedicated).
- Agree on receipt format (signed PDF + event webhook).

I attached the API spec with event payloads (deletion-api-spec.yaml). Happy to jump on the call Camila suggested.

—Marcus
